issues.failure_explanation: The supplied nonexpansivity calculation is specific to the circle. For a smooth simply connected nonconvex domain, the Laplace double-layer kernel k(x,y) can have a negative part, although its signed boundary integral is 1/2. Consequently the sup-norm operator norm of the BIE's linear part is 2 sup_x ∫|k(x,y)|dσ_y, which exceeds 1 when such a negative part occurs. The nonexpansive-operator justification therefore does not extend to the advertised arbitrary geometries, even where a pure double-layer representation exists.

issues.title: Arbitrary-geometry applicability is not supported by the nonexpansivity argument

We note that the approaches developed are applicable to any type of geometry for the domain and corresponding boundary.

issues.failure_explanation: No topological restriction on Ω is imposed. On the smooth annulus a<|x|<1, take ψ=0 and u(x)=log|x|, with its corresponding Dirichlet data. The rotational average of a Laplace double-layer potential over the two boundary circles is constant throughout the annulus: a constant outer-circle density produces a constant there, while a constant inner-circle density produces zero outside that circle. It therefore cannot equal the nonconstant radial function log|x|. The asserted representation is not surjective on this allowed domain.

issues.failure_explanation: For fixed n and q<1, the entire right side tends to zero as M grows. diagnostic_evidence.quote: where for the last steps we recall that the normal derivative of the fundamental solution is non-negative (see calculations for the potential above).

issues.failure_explanation: Nonnegativity of each normal derivative does not imply nonnegativity of their difference. The estimate requires ∫|DΦ|, not the absolute value of its signed integral. This distinction occurs even on the disk for the modified Helmholtz kernel: for sufficiently large positive λ, the normal derivative near the center is small, while its boundary-diagonal limit remains 1/(4π), so DΦ is negative near y=x*. On general nonconvex domains even the individual normal derivative need not be nonnegative.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use absolute-kernel integral bounds. In the disk setting, an alternative local bypass is to bound the total density error directly through the original double-layer operator before separating quadrature errors.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed termwise proof does not establish the stated density-error coefficient.
issues.title: The error proof drops absolute values from a potentially sign-changing difference kernel

issues.failure_explanation: The implemented representation's fourth term is evaluated at x*, but D_4 and the corresponding proof step use x. This is not harmless for the uniform interior norm. On the Poisson disk, as x=r y_j approaches a quadrature node radially, the sampled kernel equals 1/[2π(1−r)]. For a nonzero nodal density, the raw quadrature diverges while the exact double-layer potential remains bounded. Thus D_4(Ω) is generally infinite, even for a constant density, although the actual boundary-evaluated fourth term has finite quadrature error.
